study.title: Effects of noise on cochlear potentials and endolymph potassium concentration recorded with potassium-selective electrodes

caption_transcriptions.fig3: Endolymph potassium concentration and EP changes recorded simultaneously from the basal cochlear turn of a normal guinea pig during 115 dBA noise exposure. Broad-band noise was presented for three 20-min periods as indicated by horizontal bars.
caption_transcriptions.fig5: EP changes recorded from the basal turn of three different guinea pigs during the first 20 min period of exposure to 95, 105 or 115 dBA broad-band noise. Subsequent exposure to the same intensity of noise did not generate similar changes. The terms ΔEPon, ΔEPoff, ΔEPe, ΔEPo are explained in the text.

method_context.animal: Guinea pig; the illustrated Fig. 3 animal is described as normal. Fig. 5 shows three different guinea pigs, one representative trace at each sound level.
method_context.measurement_location: Basal cochlear turn; potassium-sensitive double-barrel microelectrode inserted into scala media through the spiral ligament.
method_context.ep_measurement: The potential barrel records scala-media DC potential relative to an Ag-AgCl ground electrode in the neck muscle. In Fig. 3, EP and potassium are recorded simultaneously.
method_context.potassium_measurement: The potassium-dependent potential is recorded differentially between the ion barrel and potential barrel. Electrodes were calibrated in 50-200 mM KCl at 39 ± 2 °C; mean sensitivity 58.5 mV per tenfold K change and K/Na selectivity ratio >40. The electrode responds to ionic activity; the article reports concentration assuming the activity coefficient is unchanged.
method_context.sound: Broad-band noise, levels stated in dBA, delivered to the open bulla by a horn speaker; the condenser earphone remained in the earbar throughout. A speaker replaced it for the separate closed-system octave-band protocol.
method_context.fig3_schedule: Three 20-min exposures at 115 dBA; the plotted bars and labeled time axis place them at approximately 0-20, 30-50, and 60-80 min. The two plotted quiet intervals are therefore 10 min each. Preserve the chart-derived schedule for this record; do not substitute the article's usual 5-min interval or its occasional 10-min intervals from other experiments.
method_context.fig5_schedule: The three records are the first 20-min exposure at 95, 105, or 115 dBA. Only the exposure-duration bar and 5 mV vertical scale bar are printed; there are no numbered time or absolute EP axes.

article_context.fig3_replication: The text identifies Fig. 3 as one guinea pig. Similar potassium changes were observed in six experiments and summarized separately in Table I; the plotted trajectory is not a group mean.
article_context.fig5_sample_unit: Three different guinea pigs are illustrated, one at each intensity. These are example records, not a group-average curve. The caption says subsequent exposure at the same intensity did not generate similar changes.

pre_exposure_ep.note: The article gives this overall basal-turn pre-exposure statistic near the Fig. 5 discussion; it is not the baseline of any individually digitized Fig. 5 trace.

fig5_textual_group_summaries.note: The text says the onset-off difference became more negative, resulting in very little rise in post-exposure EP; it does not give a numeric mean for that difference here.

aep_definitions.delta_ep_on: Rapid EP fall associated with noise onset.
aep_definitions.delta_ep_off: Rapid EP increase associated with noise termination.
aep_definitions.delta_ep_e: Slower EP change during exposure, excluding onset and offset components.
aep_definitions.delta_ep_o: Post-exposure EP change with noise off relative to the pre-exposure value.
aep_definitions.delta_ep_q: EP change during the quiet period between successive exposures.

digitization_method.description: Manual centerline/marker digitization from the unmodified source PDF rendered at 3 px per PDF point. The page renders and figure crops are retained and checksummed above. Coordinates refer to the upper-left origin of the named crop PNG; add the listed crop origin to obtain full-page raster coordinates.
digitization_method.uncertainty_note: These are conservative digitization/localization bounds, not biological error bars or confidence intervals. Figure 3 approximate propagated uncertainty is ±0.4 min, ±0.3 mV EP, and ±0.5 mM K. Figure 5 approximate uncertainty is ±0.3 min within the exposure and ±0.25 mV relative EP. Original trace thickness, print quality, axis-anchor selection, and line overlap limit precision.
digitization_method.correlation_warning: Adjacent digitized points along a plotted line are highly correlated and do not increase the animal/sample size. Do not treat them as independent observations or as measured raw recordings.
digitization_method.event_handling: Abrupt onset/offset steps are retained as event annotations and adjacent pre/post samples. Do not interpolate a smooth curve through these discontinuities. Fig. 3's repeated exposure and quiet segments are retained; Fig. 5's post-offset horizontal spacing is not assigned time.

horizontal_axis.mapping: Least-squares linear calibration through the printed 0, 20, 40, 60, and 80 min tick centers. The plotted trace extends to the left and right of labeled ticks; coordinates outside labeled ticks are extrapolations along the visibly linear axis.

ep.sample_unit: one illustrated individual guinea pig; basal turn; simultaneous with K+ trace

vertical_axis.mapping: Least-squares linear calibration through printed left-axis ticks.

endolymph_k.sample_unit: same illustrated individual as Fig. 3 EP; basal turn; simultaneous measurement

vertical_axis.mapping: Least-squares linear calibration through printed right-axis ticks.

horizontal_axis.mapping: Linear mapping of the printed 20-min exposure-duration bar. This supports relative time only within the exposure. Do not assign numerical times to the pre-exposure lead-in or post-offset tail, whose horizontal spacing is not separately calibrated.

vertical_scale.mapping: Relative EP change = (individual trace baseline y pixel - sampled y pixel) * 5 / (bottom_pixel - top_pixel). Smaller y pixel means higher EP.

events.note: Onset step is co-located with the exposure-bar start to within raster localization uncertainty.

95_dba.sample_unit: one illustrated individual guinea pig; basal turn; not a group mean

105_dba.sample_unit: one illustrated individual guinea pig; basal turn; not a group mean

115_dba.sample_unit: one illustrated individual guinea pig; basal turn; not a group mean

fit_use.status: source extraction only; no model fitting performed
fit_use.recommendation: These records can be included as individual-trajectory fitting targets only if the model comparison preserves the individual-trace nature and source uncertainty. Fig. 3 is one individual with simultaneous absolute EP and K; Fig. 5 contributes one example EP trajectory at each level, relative to each trace's own pre-exposure baseline. Keep the separately reported group means as distinct targets; do not substitute them for digitized examples.
fit_use.consumer: Run `python src/salt_1979_digitize.py --points` from the project root, or import `calibrated_points` from `src.salt_1979_digitize.py`. Output rows retain crop pixel x/y, calibrated time where the source permits it, calibrated measurement, units, uncertainty, phase, and discontinuity flags. Fig. 5 post-offset time remains null by design.
not_supported: Treating the dense digitized points as independent biological replicates.
Assigning an absolute EP baseline to Fig. 5 from the overall 85.0 ± 3.5 mV group statistic.
Assigning numerical post-offset times to Fig. 5.
Treating Fig. 3's single-animal trace as a group mean or extracting a group-level K trajectory.
Using the three Fig. 5 traces as repeated measurements from the same animal.
